## What it is

The Access Control policy states what the organization requires for access control and who is accountable for it. It meets [AC-1](/controls/ac/ac-1/) through the sections every family policy shares, and adds one statement group per control. Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 73 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Decision | Controls | Typical | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Which account types are allowed on each system, and which are prohibited? | [AC-2](/controls/ac/ac-2/) | Individual, privileged, service and emergency accounts allowed with a named owner; shared and guest accounts prohibited unless the system owner approves an exception. | System owner |
| Which remote access methods are allowed, and for whom? | [AC-17](/controls/ac/ac-17/), [AC-17(3)](/controls/ac/ac-17/#ac-17.3) | An organization-managed VPN or zero trust access service with multifactor authentication for all remote users; no remote desktop exposed directly to the internet. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Which identity provider is the authoritative source for accounts? | [AC-2](/controls/ac/ac-2/) | The organization's central directory or identity provider, fed by the human resources system. | Chief Information Security Officer |

Record your values in the [Access Control decision worksheet](/templates/worksheets/ac/), which lists every parameter with its typical value.

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The sections before and after Policy statements meet AC-1, which asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle. Assessors check each element, so keep every section even when it is short. Each statement cites the AC-1 item it meets. If you adopt several family policies, the same sections repeat in each; that is expected, and it lets each policy stand alone.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for Access Control, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level</span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (AC-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (AC-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (AC-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (AC-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (AC-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (AC-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Procedures

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall ensure that documented procedures exist to implement this policy and its associated controls. (AC-1a.2)

### Dissemination

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the access control policy is to be disseminated</span>. (AC-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate the procedures that implement this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the access control procedures are to be disseminated</span>. (AC-1a)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one control or enhancement in the chosen baseline. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets.
:::

#### Account management (AC-2)

:::note[Guidance]
AC-2 makes account management a controlled life cycle: every account has a known type, an owner, an approval and a removal trigger. Each statement below maps to one lettered item of the control. Assessors test these by sampling account requests, recent departures and the last access review, so keep the records each statement implies.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall define and document, for each system, the account types allowed and the account types prohibited. (AC-2a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall assign one or more account managers for each system. (AC-2b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall require <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a completed access request, a signed access agreement and completed security awareness training</span></span> before granting group or role membership. (AC-2c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall record, for each account, the authorized user, group and role membership, access authorizations and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: attributes (as required) for each account <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: an expiration date for temporary accounts, and time-of-day or location restrictions where the system supports them</span></span>. (AC-2d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall create an account only after approval by <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles required to approve requests to create accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the user's supervisor, plus the system owner or data owner for privileged roles</span></span>. (AC-2e)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall create, enable, modify, disable and remove accounts in accordance with this policy and the account management procedure. (AC-2f)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall monitor the use of accounts for activity that does not match the account's type or authorization. (AC-2g)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Supervisor</span> shall notify the account manager and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be notified <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the system security officer</span></span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to notify account managers when accounts are no longer required <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 5 business days</span></span> when a user's account is no longer required. (AC-2h.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Human resources office</span> shall notify the account manager and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be notified <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the system security officer</span></span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to notify account managers when users are terminated or transferred <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 24 hours, or the same day for privileged users</span></span> when a user is terminated or transferred. (AC-2h.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Supervisor</span> shall notify the account manager and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be notified <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the system security officer</span></span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to notify account managers when system usage or the need to know changes for an individual <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 5 business days</span></span> when a user's system usage or need to know changes. (AC-2h.3)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall authorize access only on the basis of a valid access authorization, the intended system usage and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: attributes needed to authorize system access (as required) <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: time-of-day, day-of-week or network location restrictions, where needed</span></span>. (AC-2i)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review all accounts on the system for compliance with this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency of account review <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: quarterly for privileged accounts and at least annually for all other accounts</span></span>. (AC-2j)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall disable or remove each account the review finds is no longer authorized. (AC-2j)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall change the authenticators of a shared or group account when an individual is removed from the group. (AC-2k)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall ensure account management processes are aligned with personnel termination and transfer processes. (AC-2l)

:::note[Guidance]
Where the organization does not use shared or group accounts, keep the AC-2k statement and note in the system security plan that none are deployed; the assessor will still ask. Evidence for AC-2l is usually an automated feed from the human resources system to the identity provider, or a documented handoff in the [onboarding, transfer and termination checklist](/templates/forms/onboarding-transfer-and-termination-checklist/) (PS-4).
:::

#### Automated system account management (AC-2(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall support the management of system accounts using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms used to support the management of system accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the organization's identity provider and its provisioning workflows</span></span>. (AC-2(1))

#### Automated temporary and emergency account management (AC-2(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system automatically <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one: remove; disable <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: disable</span></span> temporary and emergency accounts after <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period after which to automatically remove or disable temporary or emergency accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 72 hours for emergency accounts, and the end date approved at creation for temporary accounts</span></span>. (AC-2(2))

#### Disable accounts (AC-2(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall disable an account within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to disable accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 1 business day</span></span> when the account has expired. (AC-2(3)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall disable an account within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to disable accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 1 business day</span></span> when it is no longer associated with a user or individual. (AC-2(3)(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall disable an account within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to disable accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 1 business day</span></span> when it is in violation of organizational policy. (AC-2(3)(c))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system disables an account that has been inactive for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period for account inactivity before disabling <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 90 days</span></span>. (AC-2(3)(d))

#### Automated audit actions (AC-2(4))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system automatically audits account creation, modification, enabling, disabling and removal actions. (AC-2(4))

#### Inactivity logout (AC-2(5))

- Each user shall log out <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period of expected inactivity or description of when to log out <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at the end of each work session, and when leaving the device unattended for longer than the device lock period</span></span>. (AC-2(5))

#### Disable accounts for high-risk individuals (AC-2(13))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall disable the accounts of an individual within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to disable accounts of individuals who are discovered to pose significant risk <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 1 hour</span></span> of discovery of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: significant risks leading to disabling accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: credible indicators of insider threat, or notice of an adverse personnel action</span></span>. (AC-2(13))

#### Access enforcement (AC-3)

:::note[Guidance]
AC-3 is enforced by the system, not by people: the statement makes the system owner accountable for configuring it. Assessors check that the roles and permissions in the system match the access authorizations approved under AC-2.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system enforces approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with this policy. (AC-3)

#### Information flow enforcement (AC-4)

:::note[Guidance]
Information flow enforcement decides where information may go, not who may see it: firewall and proxy rules, cross-domain and data loss prevention filters, and cloud network policies. The [Boundary Protection Standard](/templates/standards/boundary-protection-standard/) holds the rules; interconnection agreements (CA-3) approve flows to other systems.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system enforces approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information flow control policies within the system and between connected systems <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the boundary protection standard and the approved interconnection agreements</span></span>. (AC-4)

#### Separation of duties (AC-5)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify and document <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: duties of individuals requiring separation <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: requesting and approving access; developing and deploying code to production; administering a system and reviewing its audit logs</span></span>. (AC-5a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall define system access authorizations that support separation of those duties. (AC-5b)

#### Least privilege (AC-6)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure users, and processes acting on behalf of users, are granted only the access necessary to accomplish their assigned organizational tasks. (AC-6)

#### Authorize access to security functions (AC-6(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize access to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: security functions (deployed in hardware, software, and firmware) <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: account management, audit configuration, security settings and cryptographic key management</span></span> only for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: individuals and roles with authorized access to security functions and security-relevant information <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system administrators and security personnel named in the system security plan</span></span>. (AC-6(1)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize access to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: security-relevant information for authorized access <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: audit logs, security configuration settings and access control lists</span></span> only for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: individuals and roles with authorized access to security functions and security-relevant information <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system administrators and security personnel named in the system security plan</span></span>. (AC-6(1)(b))

#### Non-privileged access for nonsecurity functions (AC-6(2))

- Users of accounts or roles with access to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: security functions or security-relevant information, the access to which requires users to use non-privileged accounts to access non-security functions, <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the security functions and security-relevant information authorized under AC-6(1)</span></span> shall use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions such as email and web browsing. (AC-6(2))

#### Privileged accounts (AC-6(5))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall restrict privileged accounts on the system to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to which privileged accounts on the system are to be restricted <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system administrators named in the system security plan</span></span>. (AC-6(5))

#### Review of user privileges (AC-6(7))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review the privileges assigned to roles or classes of users <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: quarterly for privileged roles and at least annually for all other roles</span></span> the privileges assigned to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: roles or classes of users to which privileges are assigned <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: all roles and classes of users on the system</span></span> to validate the need for them. (AC-6(7)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall reassign or remove privileges the review finds are not needed for the user's mission and business functions. (AC-6(7)(b))

#### Log use of privileged functions (AC-6(9))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system logs the execution of privileged functions. (AC-6(9))

#### Prohibit non-privileged users from executing privileged functions (AC-6(10))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions. (AC-6(10))

#### Unsuccessful logon attempts (AC-7)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system enforces a limit of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the number of consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user allowed during a time period <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 3</span></span> consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period to which the number of consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user is limited <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 15 minutes</span></span>. (AC-7a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system automatically takes the following action when the limit is exceeded: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: lock the account or node for [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; lock the account or node until released by an administrator; delay next logon prompt per [Assignment: organization-defined delay algorithm]; notify system administrator; take other [Assignment: organization-defined action] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: lock the account or node for 30 minutes, or until released by an administrator for privileged accounts</span></span>. (AC-7b)

#### System use notification (AC-8)

:::note[Guidance]
The banner text is usually approved once by legal counsel and reused on every system. The four notices listed in AC-8a are written for U.S. Government systems; the statements below keep the ones that apply to any organization and move the two government-only notices to the federal section.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system displays <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: system use notification message or banner to be displayed by the system to users before granting access to the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the organization's approved logon banner</span></span> to users before granting access. (AC-8a)
- The notice shall state that system usage may be monitored, recorded and subject to audit; that unauthorized use of the system is prohibited; and that use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording. (AC-8a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the notice remains on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit action to log on to or further access the system. (AC-8b)
- For publicly accessible systems, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system displays system use information <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: conditions for system use to be displayed by the system before granting further access <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: on the landing page, before users submit any information</span></span>, before granting further access. (AC-8c.1)
- For publicly accessible systems, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure any references to monitoring, recording or auditing are consistent with the privacy accommodations for such systems. (AC-8c.2)
- For publicly accessible systems, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the notice describes the authorized uses of the system. (AC-8c.3)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AC-8a requires the notice on federal systems to state two more things ([AC-8](/controls/ac/ac-8/)).

- The notice shall state that users are accessing a U.S. Government system. (AC-8a.1)
- The notice shall state that unauthorized use of the system is subject to criminal and civil penalties. (AC-8a.3)

</div>

#### Device lock (AC-11)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system prevents further access by <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: initiating a device lock after [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of inactivity; requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: initiating a device lock after 15 minutes of inactivity, and requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended</span></span>. (AC-11a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the device lock remains until the user reestablishes access using the established identification and authentication procedures. (AC-11b)

#### Pattern-hiding displays (AC-11(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the device lock conceals information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image. (AC-11(1))

#### Session termination (AC-12)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system automatically terminates a user session after <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: conditions or trigger events requiring session disconnect <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 30 minutes of inactivity for remote and web sessions, or at the end of the maximum session lifetime</span></span>. (AC-12)

#### Permitted actions without identification or authentication (AC-14)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: user actions that can be performed on the system without identification or authentication <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: viewing public web pages and the logon page</span></span> as the only user actions that can be performed on the system without identification or authentication. (AC-14a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall document those actions, with the supporting rationale, in the system security plan. (AC-14b)

#### Remote access (AC-17)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall establish and document usage restrictions, configuration and connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed. (AC-17a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize each type of remote access to the system before allowing such connections. (AC-17b)

#### Remote access monitoring and control (AC-17(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ automated mechanisms to monitor and control remote access methods. (AC-17(1))

#### Protection of confidentiality and integrity using encryption (AC-17(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure cryptographic mechanisms protect the confidentiality and integrity of remote access sessions. (AC-17(2))

#### Managed access control points (AC-17(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure remote access is routed through authorized and managed network access control points. (AC-17(3))

#### Remote privileged commands and access (AC-17(4))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize the execution of privileged commands via remote access only for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: needs requiring execution of privileged commands via remote access <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: emergency administration outside business hours and administration of cloud-hosted components</span></span>, and only in a format that provides assessable evidence. (AC-17(4)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize access to security-relevant information via remote access only for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: needs requiring access to security-relevant information via remote access <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: investigation of security incidents</span></span>, and only in a format that provides assessable evidence. (AC-17(4)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall document the rationale for such remote access in the system security plan. (AC-17(4)(b))

#### Wireless access (AC-18)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall establish configuration requirements, connection requirements and implementation guidance for each type of wireless access. (AC-18a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize each type of wireless access to the system before allowing such connections. (AC-18b)

#### Wireless authentication and encryption (AC-18(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall protect wireless access to the system using authentication of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: users; devices <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: users and devices</span></span> and encryption. (AC-18(1))

#### Disable wireless networking (AC-18(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure wireless networking capabilities embedded in system components are disabled before issuance and deployment when not intended for use. (AC-18(3))

#### Access control for mobile devices (AC-19)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall establish configuration requirements, connection requirements and implementation guidance for organization-controlled mobile devices, including when devices are outside controlled areas. (AC-19a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize the connection of mobile devices to the system. (AC-19b)

#### Full device or container-based encryption (AC-19(5))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall require <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one: full-device encryption; container-based encryption <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: full-device encryption</span></span> to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: mobile devices on which to employ encryption <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: all organization-controlled mobile devices</span></span>. (AC-19(5))

#### Use of external systems (AC-20)

- Before authorized individuals access the system from an external system, or process, store or transmit organization-controlled information on one, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: establish [Assignment: organization-defined terms and conditions]; identify [Assignment: organization-defined controls asserted] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: establish terms and conditions in a signed agreement with the organization that owns the external system</span></span>, consistent with the trust relationship with the organization that owns, operates or maintains the external system. (AC-20a)
- Users shall not use <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: types of external systems prohibited from use <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: personally owned devices that the organization does not manage, and public or shared computers</span></span> to access the system or to process, store or transmit organization-controlled information. (AC-20b)

#### Limits on authorized use (AC-20(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall permit authorized individuals to use an external system to access the system, or to process, store or transmit organization-controlled information, only after the controls on the external system are verified against the organization's policies and plans, or an approved connection or processing agreement is in place with its owner. (AC-20(1))

#### Portable storage devices: restricted use (AC-20(2))

- Authorized individuals shall use organization-controlled portable storage devices on external systems only under <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: restrictions on the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: use only of encrypted, organization-issued devices, and only for approved business purposes</span></span>. (AC-20(2))

#### Information sharing (AC-21)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall enable authorized users to determine whether the access authorizations of a sharing partner match the information's access and use restrictions for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information-sharing circumstances where user discretion is required to determine whether access authorizations assigned to a sharing partner match the information’s access and use restrictions <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: sharing sensitive or contract-restricted information with partners outside the organization</span></span>. (AC-21a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms or manual processes that assist users in making information-sharing and collaboration decisions <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: information labels and a data-sharing checklist</span></span> to assist users in making information sharing and collaboration decisions. (AC-21b)

#### Publicly accessible content (AC-22)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall designate the individuals authorized to make information publicly accessible. (AC-22a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure those individuals are trained to keep nonpublic information out of publicly accessible content. (AC-22b)
- The designated individuals shall review proposed content for nonpublic information before posting it on the publicly accessible system. (AC-22c)
- The designated individuals shall review the content on the publicly accessible system for nonpublic information <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review the content on the publicly accessible system for non-public information <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: quarterly</span></span>. (AC-22d)
- The designated individuals shall remove nonpublic information when a review discovers it. (AC-22d)

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall review and update this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current access control policy is reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the current access control policy to be reviewed and updated</span>. (AC-1c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall review and update the procedures that implement this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current access control procedures are reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require procedures to be reviewed and updated</span>. (AC-1c.2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal information systems, this policy also carries out the agency's information security responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim), Federal agency responsibilities) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- Where the agency's organization-wide policy sets a value for a parameter in this policy, each system shall use that value or a stricter one. (AC-1a.1(b))

</div>
